correctness.rationale: Direct comparison of the printed uncontrolled and controlled state equations proves the unit-control mismatch: for positive \(ASI\), \(\lambda SI/(1+A)=\lambda SI/(1+cA)\) only if \(c=1\). Direct summation of the printed human compartments gives \(\dot N=\Pi-dN-\delta(I+Q+H)+(1-u_1)A(r_1I+r_2Q+r_3H)\). Exact source-parameter witnesses give incidence values \(1/44\) and \(1/48\), and an artificial source \(7/400\). Differentiation of the minimally repaired Hamiltonian forces the recovered-state costate into the \(u_1\) stationarity law.

value.rationale: The defect affects the mathematical object optimized in the paper rather than a peripheral calculation. The unit-control limit changes the incidence law used to compare controlled and uncontrolled trajectories; the unmatched recovery control adds a nonphysical source to total human population; and repairing that transfer changes the first-order treatment-control condition. The result supplies exact diagnostics and a minimal correction, making it useful for any reuse or numerical reproduction of the model.
